content: 1. Hyoscyamine and Imipramine: Both drugs reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. This can lead to additive anticholinergic effects, including potential hypoglycemia. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Methylene Blue and Imipramine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels, which can lead to serotonin syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If methylene blue must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Serotonergic therapy can be resumed 24 hours after the last methylene blue dose or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 3. Hyoscyamine and IncobotulinumtoxinA: Hyoscyamine enhances the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Close monitoring is advised. 4.
